references.text: The Ten Commandments in [ref:Exod 20:12-16|Exodus 20:12-16] are the source Jesus quotes from. He restates the commandments against adultery, murder, theft, false witness, and honoring father and mother.
[ref:Deut 5:16-20|Deuteronomy 5:16-20] contains the repeated version of the Ten Commandments in Deuteronomy, with the same commandments Jesus quotes here.
"Μὴ μοιχεύσῃς" – "You shall not commit adultery" – is a direct quote from the sixth commandment in [ref:Exod 20:14|Exodus 20:14].
"Μὴ φονεύσῃς" – "You shall not murder" – is a direct quote from the fifth commandment in [ref:Exod 20:13|Exodus 20:13].
"Μὴ κλέψῃς" – "You shall not steal" – is a direct quote from the seventh commandment in [ref:Exod 20:15|Exodus 20:15].
"Μὴ ψευδομαρτυρήσῃς" – "You shall not bear false witness" – is a direct quote from the eighth commandment in [ref:Exod 20:16|Exodus 20:16].
"Τίμα τὸν πατέρα σου καὶ τὴν μητέρα" – "Honor your father and your mother" – is a direct quote from the fourth commandment in [ref:Exod 20:12|Exodus 20:12].
The commandment "You shall not commit adultery" is repeated in [ref:Deut 5:18|Deuteronomy 5:18].
The commandment "You shall not murder" is repeated in [ref:Deut 5:17|Deuteronomy 5:17].
The parallel passage in [ref:Matt 19:18-19|Matthew 19:18-19] recounts the same conversation with the rich young man, where Jesus lists the same commandments.
The parallel passage in [ref:Mark 10:19|Mark 10:19] also records Jesus' listing of the commandments to the rich man.
Paul summarizes the same commandments in [ref:Rom 13:9|Romans 13:9] and says that they are all summed up in the command to love your neighbor as yourself.
James refers to the commandments against adultery and murder in [ref:Jas 2:11|James 2:11] and emphasizes that whoever breaks one commandment is guilty of all.
